 Driving in wintry weather can be dangerous and challenging, so it's important for drivers to be prepared 
 Winters in Northern Nevada can be harsh, and conditions can change quickly. 
 Both NDOT and drivers we spoke with suggest traveling only when necessary during a storm, and to make sure to leave early to give yourself enough time to reach your destination. 
 Eric Corona, a driver we spoke with, told us, "Drive cautiously. Just make sure you check your tires and make sure that where you're going, you have a plan and a little bit extra time. Just for traffic. If you're going to make a left-hand turn in a couple of blocks, stick on the left-hand lane and just plan ahead." 
 It’s a good idea to have a safety kit in your car specifically designed for the winter. This can include snow chains, snacks, and blankets. 
 Corona shared a tip with us that he found helpful if you find yourself stuck in the snow. 
 "It sounds a little off, but kitty litter soaks up a lot of the moisture in the snow. Helps to get traction and get out of whatever spots you're in. So, I mean, and then I'll settle with the essentials. Batteries, flashlights, and things of that nature. But, yeah, I really try to stick to kitty litter and water,” said Corona. 
 Using extra caution on bridges, ramps, overpasses, and shaded areas that may freeze is a good thing to remember. 
 Avoiding quick stops and fast turns can be the thing that helps keep you and other drivers safe on the road. 
 Make sure you keep your gas tank full as well in case you get stuck in traffic. 
 Drivers say if you aren't sure about winter driving, then staying home might be the smart thing to do. 
 Kelli Morales, another driver we spoke to, told us, "Confidence does go a long way while driving in any weather at all, but mostly in the snow and rain. If you question yourself, it's probably not a good idea, but if you have the confidence, that's much better." 
 It can be an expensive purchase, but making sure you have good tires heading into the winter will also help keep you safe when driving. 
 And making sure your wipers and headlights are working before you head out is also a good idea.
